Next, we discuss the Machine Learning period, which standardized the RFF workflow around feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, and supervised classification, followed by the Deep Learning period, in which representation learning from raw IQ samples significantly improved performance and expanded the application space. Beyond a chronological list of methods and best practices, this paper critically examines the changing assumptions and persistent limitations that have driven these transitions. We highlight the central challenges that continue to shape the field, including channel dependence, receiver sensitivity, limited dataset realism, poor cross-domain generalization, open-set recognition, and adversarial robustness. By organizing more than three decades of work into a coherent narrative, this paper clarifies the evolution of RFF, identifies persistent limitations, and outlines the key research directions required to move the field toward dependable real-world adoption.
tldr: A historical survey of radio frequency fingerprinting (RFF) for wireless device identification, covering paradigm shifts from 1993 to 2026.
motivation: To provide a critical historical analysis of RFF, clarifying its evolution and persistent limitations to guide future research.
method: Organizes RFF research into conceptual phases: transient-based, steady-state, machine learning, and deep learning, with critical examination of assumptions and challenges.
result: Identifies key challenges such as channel dependence, dataset realism, cross-domain generalization, and adversarial robustness.
conclusion: RFF has matured but still faces fundamental obstacles; future work must address these for dependable real-world adoption.

title: Graft: Graphlet-Triggered Backdoor Attack On GNN-Based Hardware Security Systems
authors: Sai Manoj Pudukotai Dinakarrao Sanaz Kazemi Abharian
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The globalization of the integrated circuit (IC) supply chain increases the risk of security threats, such as hardware Trojans (HTs) and the theft of intellectual property (IP). Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), among the most powerful deep learning methods for processing graph-structured data, have been widely adopted to detect such threats. However, GNNs are susceptible to backdoor attacks that can maliciously manipulate output predictions toward an adversarial target. These attacks are not only difficult to detect but also compromise the integrity of GNN-based security systems. Most prior work embeds backdoor triggers using randomly generated subgraphs or gradient-guided generative subgraphs. However, such triggers are impractical for GNN-based hardware security applications as they do not guarantee the preservation of circuit functionality. In this paper, we propose GRAFT, a graph let-triggered backdoor attack targeting GNN-based hardware security. GRAFT embeds graphlet-based triggers at either the register-transfer level (RTL) or gate level of the design while preserving the circuit 's original function. We evaluate GRAFT on the ISCAS-85 and TrustHub datasets. Our experimental results demonstrate that GRAFT can effectively evade HT detection and IP piracy detection, achieving an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 100%.
tldr: This paper proposes a graphlet-triggered backdoor attack on GNN-based hardware security systems, focusing on hardware Trojan detection and IP piracy.
motivation: GNN-based hardware security systems are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and existing triggers are impractical as they do not preserve circuit functionality.
method: The authors embed graphlet-based triggers at RTL or gate level while preserving the circuit's original function, and evaluate on ISCAS-85 and TrustHub datasets.
result: The attack achieves up to 100% attack success rate in evading HT detection and IP piracy detection.
conclusion: GRAFT demonstrates a practical backdoor attack that compromises GNN-based hardware security, highlighting the need for robust defenses.

title: When Vr Meets Bci: (Un)Observable Brainwave-aware Privacy Reconstruction In The Metaverse Via Unrestricted Inbuilt Motion Sensors
authors: Tao Ni, Zehua Sun, Qingchuan Zhao, Wei-Bin Lee, Cong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metaverse devices, such as virtual reality (VR), have seen substantial development and widespread applications in numerous areas. Although recent studies have revealed privacy leakages in VR, these vulnerabilities were limited in the scope of observable behaviors in virtual scenes (e.g., what a user is seeing). In this work, we uncover the feasibility of going beyond the scope of observable user behaviors to unobservable brain EEG-correlated representations (e.g., what a user is perceiving) by leveraging unrestricted motion sensors in VR headsets to reconstruct brain EEG signals, a seemingly neglected but promising vector. The insight is that the inbuilt motion sensors (e.g., accelerometers) in the VR headset can capture subtle vibrations induced by pupillary responses, which are highly correlated with users' visual stimuli and in-brain perceptions. Therefore, we design and implement BraVeSpy to systematically investigate and demonstrate the feasibility of this severe privacy leakage originating from brain EEG-correlated representations reconstructed from variations of inbuilt motion sensors. Our extensive evaluation results from different VR devices show that BraVeSpy, for the first time in the Metaverse, can reveal unobservable privacy, where we successfully unveiled perceptive images in the brain with 52.0%-67.2% accuracy. In particular, we also find that BraVeSpy outperforms the current approaches that are limited to coarse-grained inference of observable behaviors and achieves over 85.0% accuracy in inferring user activity-related sensitive information, such as fingerprinting websites, apps, and streaming videos, and over 96.0% accuracy in user de-anonymization, gaze movement tracking, and virtual keystroke inference.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a privacy attack in VR that reconstructs brain EEG signals from motion sensor vibrations, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To show that VR motion sensors can capture brainwave-correlated vibrations, enabling privacy leakage beyond observable behaviors.
method: Uses accelerometers in VR headsets to measure subtle vibrations from pupillary responses, then reconstructs EEG-correlated signals to infer visual stimuli and user activities.
result: Achieves 52-67% accuracy in reconstructing perceptive images and over 85% accuracy in inferring activities like website fingerprinting and keystroke inference.
conclusion: VR motion sensors pose a severe privacy risk by enabling brainwave-aware reconstruction, highlighting the need for countermeasures.

title: A Deployment-Oriented Framework For Explainable AI-Assisted eBPF/XDP Mitigation At The IoT Edge
authors: Abdurrahman Tolay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) deployments combine heterogeneous, resource-constrained devices with weak security configurations, exposed services, limited logging, patching constraints, and long lifecycles. Signature- and threshold-based controls remain useful baselines, but they are insufficient as standalone mechanisms in dynamic IoT networks. Likewise, offline artificial intelligence (AI) benchmark performance alone does not establish operational deployability. This article presents a conceptual framework and research agenda for a Linux-based IoT edge gateway that combines resource-aware flow-level AI-assisted risk scoring, event-level explainability, and bounded mitigation through eBPF/XDP. The controller applies reversible, time-limited actions subject to critical-device safeguards, updates packet-level enforcement state, and records structured logs. The architecture separates complex reasoning and policy control in user space from concise packet-handling decisions in the kernel. It also defines a future hardware-aware evaluation pathway covering detection quality, resource cost, response timing, rollback behaviour, and legitimate-traffic preservation. The paper does not report new experimental meas.
tldr: A conceptual framework for AI-assisted mitigation at the IoT edge using eBPF/XDP, with no experimental results.
motivation: IoT devices are vulnerable and traditional security measures are insufficient; AI can help but must be deployable on resource-constrained hardware.
method: Proposes a Linux-based IoT edge gateway architecture combining flow-level AI risk scoring, event-level explainability, and eBPF/XDP for bounded mitigation.
result: No experimental results are reported; the paper presents only a conceptual framework and future evaluation pathway.
conclusion: The framework aims to balance detection quality, resource cost, and response timing, but requires experimental validation.

title: Quantified Propositional Calculi And Narrow Implicit Proofs
authors: Neil Thapen Pavel Pudl\'ak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the implicit version of a propositional proof system Q, we work with Q-proofs that are not written down directly, but are succinctly encoded by circuits. Thus implicit Q-proofs are potentially exponentially shorter than usual Q-proofs. We study narrow implicit proofs, a restricted version of this notion, in which lines in the encoded proof can only have polynomial size. We use a cut-elimination construction to show that G_{i+1} is equivalent to narrow implicit G_i, for i >= 1, where G_i is the extension of Frege allowing reasoning with Sigma^q_i quantified propositional formulas. We show that G_1 is equivalent to implicit resolution.
tldr: The paper studies implicit propositional proofs and their equivalence to quantified propositional calculi, focusing on proof complexity rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the relationship between implicit proof systems and quantified propositional calculi, and to show that narrow implicit proofs can be exponentially shorter than standard proofs.
method: Uses cut-elimination constructions to prove equivalences between different proof systems, such as G_{i+1} and narrow implicit G_i, and G_1 with implicit resolution.
result: Establishes that G_{i+1} is equivalent to narrow implicit G_i for i >= 1, and G_1 is equivalent to implicit resolution.
conclusion: The work contributes to proof complexity theory but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Snaproot: Decentralized File Integrity Verification Using Blockchain-Anchored Cryptographic Hashing
authors: Tarkan Yavas Arslan Br\"omme
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of digital content has made reliable integrity verification increasingly important. Existing solutions rely either on centralized authorities, which introduce trust dependencies and single points of failure, or on decentralized storage systems that incur prohibitive resource overhead. In this paper, we present snaproot, a lightweight system that implements the hash-anchoring paradigm of Haber and Stornetta on the Solana blockchain to provide efficient, decentralized file integrity verification. snaproot generates a SHA-256 hash of a file and stores it immutably on-chain as a permanent reference record. Verification is performed by recomputing the hash and comparing it to the stored value, yielding a deterministic binary outcome. We describe a four-tier trust architecture comprising three realized tiers and one prospective tier for long-term persistence beyond the lifetime of any single blockchain. We present a formal threat model, a security analysis grounded in the second-preimage resistance of SHA-256, and an empirical evaluation on Solana Devnet across file sizes from 1 KB to 500 MB. A central conceptual contribution is the explicit separation between existence proof, the key-independent claim that a file existed at a given time, and authorship proof, the key-dependent binding between a record and a specific wallet identity. This separation allows existence guarantees to survive key loss while preserving stronger authorship claims where keys are retained. We position snaproot against OpenTimestamps, OriginStamp, and Chainpoint and discuss limitations with respect to pre-registration manipulation and AI-generated content.
tldr: This paper presents a blockchain-based file integrity verification system using SHA-256 hashing on Solana.
motivation: Existing centralized and decentralized integrity solutions suffer from trust dependencies or high resource overhead.
method: The system generates a SHA-256 hash of a file and stores it immutably on the Solana blockchain; verification recomputes the hash and compares it to the stored value.
result: Empirical evaluation on Solana Devnet shows feasibility across file sizes from 1 KB to 500 MB, with a formal threat model and security analysis.
conclusion: Snaproot provides lightweight, decentralized integrity verification with a clear separation between existence and authorship proofs.

title: Post-Quantum Secure Federated DeFi For Inclusive Banking
authors: Swati Sachan, Dale Fickett, Richard Buchinger, Theo Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in error-corrected qubits have accelerated the timeline for practical quantum computing. It poses a threat to cryptographic primitives used to secure financial systems, government infrastructure, communication networks, and DeFi (Decentralized Finance) ecosystems. This paper introduces a post-quantum secure federated DeFi framework that enables inter-bank collaboration to improve the inclusivity of individuals underserved by local lenders due to limited financial histories. Multiple banks contribute encrypted information batches to a virtual server, where lattice-based Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables end-to-end homomorphic computation. The server fuses local data-driven probabilistic assessments, expert beliefs, and verifiable evidence generated by the NASA-IBM Prithvi Geospatial Foundation Model (GFM), in encrypted format. Decentralized technologies are employed to ensure tamper-proof evidence and auditable accountability for all encrypted data exchanges between institutions and the server. The framework is tested on agricultural lending decisions for rural borrowers in Virginia.
tldr: A post-quantum secure federated DeFi framework using lattice-based FHE and geospatial AI for inclusive banking.
motivation: To protect DeFi systems from quantum threats and improve financial inclusion for underserved borrowers.
method: Combines lattice-based fully homomorphic encryption, federated learning, and NASA-IBM Prithvi Geospatial Foundation Model for encrypted data fusion.
result: Demonstrates feasibility on agricultural lending decisions in rural Virginia.
conclusion: The framework offers quantum-secure, privacy-preserving inter-bank collaboration for inclusive finance.

title: On Automorphic Measures, Lyapunov Exponents And Instability Of Rational Maps
authors: Carlos Cabrera Makienko Peter
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To construct obstructions to the stability of rational maps with non-summable critical points in their Julia sets, we introduce automorphic measures with complex eigenvalues for rational maps on the Riemann sphere. In particular, these measures extend the classical notions of quasi-invariant and conformal measures by allowing the respective Radon--Nikodym derivative to be complex-valued and proportional to a multiplicative cocycle. \[ j_{(s,t)}(R) = |R'|^{s} \left({R'}\right)^{t}, \] which plays the role of a generalized automorphy factor in the sense of group actions. The existence of such measures reveals a close connection between geometric and dynamical properties of rational maps. We show that the existence of certain automorphic measures, particularly unimodular measures and their associated vector fields, implies instability of the corresponding rational map. Specifically, for a weakly dissipative rational map admitting a [MATH]-unimodular measure, there exists an integer [MATH] such that the map is [MATH]-unstable. This result generalizes earlier instability criteria involving pseudoconformal measures and connects the presence of such measures to the failure of structural stability. Furthermore, we establish ergodic and combinatorial conditions ensuring the existence of unimodular measures or vector fields -- most notably, through bounded recurrence, bounded velocity of arguments, and relations with the Milnor--Thurston kneading theory. These criteria provide a unified framework linking automorphic measures, Lyapunov spectra, and the geometric deformation spaces of rational maps.
tldr: This paper studies automorphic measures and instability of rational maps in complex dynamics, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To construct obstructions to stability of rational maps with non-summable critical points in their Julia sets.
method: Introduces automorphic measures with complex eigenvalues for rational maps on the Riemann sphere, extending quasi-invariant and conformal measures.
result: Existence of certain automorphic measures implies instability of the corresponding rational map, generalizing earlier instability criteria.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework linking automorphic measures, Lyapunov spectra, and geometric deformation spaces of rational maps.

title: Integral Formulations For Two-dimensional Multi-Arcs
authors: Ruben Aylwin Jose Pinto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Laplace equation with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions posed on multi-arcs, i.e., collections of open arcs meeting at junction points. We begin by introducing a scale of Sobolev spaces constructed using the Sobolev spaces on open arcs as main building block and extend the definition of trace operators. We reformulate the boundary value problems using boundary integral formulations. We then establish a well-posed integral formulation for the Dirichlet problem, which can be discretized using standard numerical methods. We further investigate the singular behavior of the solution densities at branch points through numerical experiments and observe that these singularities are comparable to the corner singularities arising in polygonal domains. For the Neumann problem, we show that the associated hypersingular operator is not necessarily invertible on classical Sobolev spaces and provide numerical evidence that solutions may develop jump discontinuities at branch points.
tldr: This paper studies boundary integral formulations for Laplace equations on multi-arcs, focusing on well-posedness and singular behavior at junction points.
motivation: To develop rigorous integral formulations for boundary value problems on multi-arcs, which are collections of open arcs meeting at junctions, and to understand solution singularities at branch points.
method: Introduces Sobolev spaces on multi-arcs, extends trace operators, and reformulates Dirichlet and Neumann problems as boundary integral equations. Numerical experiments investigate singular behavior.
result: Establishes a well-posed integral formulation for the Dirichlet problem. For the Neumann problem, shows the hypersingular operator may not be invertible and solutions can develop jump discontinuities at branch points.
conclusion: The integral formulations provide a foundation for numerical discretization, and the observed singularities resemble corner singularities in polygonal domains.

title: Non-Euclidean Unification Of Isoperimetric Profiles And Grand Lebesgue-Sobolev Scales
authors: Alexander Zuevsky Daniel Levin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a complete separable metric measure space satisfying a doubling condition and a [MATH]-Poincar\'e inequality. We develop a rigorous framework unifying two lines of analysis: the isoperimetric-profile approach of Coulhon-Grigor'yan-Levin and the grand/small Lebesgue-Sobolev scale introduced by Fiorenza-Formica-Gogatishvili . An explicit profile-to-scale transform [MATH], defined via an inverse integral of [MATH], converts geometric data into grand Lebesgue parameters. Sharp, up to universal constants, embeddings [MATH] with explicit constants (Theorem ). A converse: controlled grand embeddings imply explicit lower bounds on [MATH] (Theorem ). Concrete examples in genuinely non-Euclidean settings: the Heisenberg group [MATH], a model manifold with logarithmic volume growth, and Gaussian measure on [MATH] treated as a locally doubling space. All arguments are carried out on general metric measure spaces without reference to charts or a smooth structure; the gradient is the upper gradient in the sense of Heinonen-Koskela, and perimeter is the outer Minkowski content.
tldr: This paper develops a unified framework connecting isoperimetric profiles and grand Lebesgue-Sobolev scales on metric measure spaces, with applications to non-Euclidean settings like the Heisenberg group.
motivation: To bridge two separate lines of analysis in geometric analysis and function space theory, providing a systematic transform between geometric and analytic quantities.
method: Defines an explicit profile-to-scale transform via an inverse integral of the isoperimetric profile, and proves sharp embeddings and converse bounds using doubling and Poincaré conditions.
result: Establishes sharp embeddings between isoperimetric and grand Lebesgue-Sobolev spaces with explicit constants, and shows that controlled grand embeddings imply lower bounds on the isoperimetric profile.
conclusion: The framework unifies geometric and analytic perspectives, with concrete examples in non-Euclidean spaces, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Branch And Price For Railway Crew Scheduling: Benchmark Instances And Computational Study
authors: Bart van Rossum
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Railway crew scheduling consists of assigning a set of tasks to crew members in the form of feasible duties so as to minimise costs, and is one of the key planning problems faced by railway operators. While column generation is the dominant solution method, literature on exact branch-and-price approaches is scarce. Moreover, few publicly available benchmark instances exist. We present a state-of-the-art branch-and-price algorithm and conduct a systematic computational study of its components, including branching rules, primal heuristics, and reduced cost fixing techniques. To this end, we introduce a novel library of 75 benchmark instances, ranging in size from 450 to 3,016 tasks. The instances are generated by mimicking the full railway planning process, validated against data from Netherlands Railways, and publicly available with best known solutions and a solution checker. We report average optimality gaps well below 1% across all instance sizes, driven primarily by the strong performance of primal heuristics, whereas branching and reduced cost fixing contribute little to closing the gap. Our findings provide support for the popularity of column generation-based primal heuristics, and show that improving the dual bound remains the main challenge for exact methods in railway crew scheduling.
tldr: This paper presents a branch-and-price algorithm for railway crew scheduling with new benchmark instances.
motivation: Railway crew scheduling is a critical operational problem, and exact branch-and-price methods are underdeveloped with few public benchmarks.
method: The authors develop a branch-and-price algorithm with branching rules, primal heuristics, and reduced cost fixing, and generate 75 benchmark instances based on Netherlands Railways data.
result: Average optimality gaps below 1% are achieved, primarily due to primal heuristics; branching and reduced cost fixing contribute little.
conclusion: Column generation-based primal heuristics are effective, but improving dual bounds remains the main challenge for exact methods.

title: Existence Of A Periodic Orbit For Billiards In Polygons
authors: Giovanni Forni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the billiard flow in any finite polygon has at least one periodic orbit. The proof by contradiction is based on a fundamental result on the dynamics of the billiard flow by Galperin, Kr\"uger and Troubetzkoy, on the geometry of a one-parameter scaling of the natural Riemannian metric on the unit tangent bundle, and on the topology of the skeleton or cut-locus of the scaled metrics.
tldr: Proves existence of at least one periodic orbit in any polygonal billiard using scaling of Riemannian metric and cut-locus topology.
motivation: Periodic orbits in polygonal billiards are fundamental to understanding dynamical systems, but existence was not proven for all polygons.
method: Proof by contradiction using Galperin-Krüger-Troubetzkoy dynamics, one-parameter scaling of the natural Riemannian metric on the unit tangent bundle, and topology of the skeleton/cut-locus.
result: Every finite polygon has at least one periodic billiard orbit.
conclusion: The result resolves a long-standing open problem in billiard dynamics.

title: The Dual Averaging Power-Prox Method With Application To Heavy-Tail Incremental Gradient
authors: Yuan Gao, Jeremy Rack, Sebastian U. Stich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-sum composite optimization under two departures from classical stochastic gradient descent theory that are central in practice: incremental gradient access and heavy-tailed gradient noise. Specifically, we consider fixed cyclic passes over component gradients and assume that, at the optimum, component gradients have a bounded [MATH]-th centralized moment for some [MATH]. This setting is much closer to modern ML training practice than the assumptions used in classical SGD theory, yet its theoretical understanding remains limited. We propose a Dual Averaging Power-Prox method for incremental gradients and establish, to the best of our knowledge, the first convergence analysis in this regime. We further show that our method achieves a better asymptotic convergence rate than the corresponding SGD method with i.i.d. (with-replacement) sampling.
tldr: This paper proposes a dual averaging method for finite-sum composite optimization with incremental gradient access and heavy-tailed noise, establishing convergence rates.
motivation: Classical SGD theory assumes i.i.d. sampling and light-tailed noise, but modern ML training often uses cyclic passes and heavy-tailed gradients, lacking theoretical guarantees.
method: The authors develop a Dual Averaging Power-Prox method that handles incremental (cyclic) gradient updates and heavy-tailed noise with bounded centralized moments.
result: They provide the first convergence analysis for this setting and show that the method achieves a better asymptotic rate than SGD with i.i.d. sampling.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a theoretically grounded optimization algorithm for practical ML training with cyclic data access and heavy-tailed noise.

title: Wing: A Simple Windowed Nonorthogonalized Initial Guess Procedure For Repeated Matrix Solves
authors: David Wells, Matthew G. Knepley, Boyce E. Griffith
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many numerical methods require solution of a sequence of linear systems with the same matrix and similar right-hand sides. Krylov subspace methods are a common tool for solving such linear systems, and a carefully chosen initial guess for the solution can reduce the total number of iterations, and thereby the total computational cost, required for convergence to a specified numerical tolerance. This paper introduces the WING algorithm, a modification of Fischer's second algorithm, which lowers the cost of forming an acceptably close initial guess by skipping orthogonalization and solving the possibly singular normal equations with a pseudoinverse. We demonstrate the efficacy of the new algorithm, particularly for solving linear systems with coarse relative tolerances, with numerical benchmarks based on fluid-structure interaction, mantle convection, and earthquake models.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical algorithm for improving initial guesses in repeated linear system solves, with applications in computational physics.
motivation: Solving sequences of linear systems with the same matrix is common in numerical simulations; a good initial guess reduces Krylov subspace iterations and computational cost.
method: The WING algorithm modifies Fischer's second algorithm by skipping orthogonalization and solving the normal equations with a pseudoinverse to form an initial guess.
result: Numerical benchmarks on fluid-structure interaction, mantle convection, and earthquake models show reduced iteration counts, especially for coarse tolerances.
conclusion: WING provides a simple, cost-effective way to generate initial guesses for repeated linear solves, improving efficiency in computational science applications.

title: Bidirectional Sddp With Dimension-free Complexity For Solving Strongly Convex Stochastic Dynamic Programming Equations
authors: Pablo Barros Vincent Guigues
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the complexity of Bidirectional Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming (BSDDP) algorithm applied to multistage stochastic optimization problems with strongly convex cost functions. Under standard regularity assumptions and without discount factor, we establish an explicit complexity bound on the expected number of iterations needed to obtain an epsilon-optimal policy. Our bound depends on the strong convexity constants and Lipschitz constants of the stagewise cost functions but is independent of the dimensionality of the state space. This improves upon the complexity of SDDP for convex problems from (Lan, 2020), particularly when the number of stages is moderate and the state dimension is large. The analysis further reveals that the complexity decreases as the strong convexity of the cost functions increases, highlighting the algorithm efficiency in structured problem instances.
tldr: This paper analyzes the complexity of a stochastic optimization algorithm (BSDDP) for strongly convex dynamic programming, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To improve the efficiency of solving multistage stochastic optimization problems with high-dimensional state spaces.
method: The authors analyze the Bidirectional Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming algorithm under strong convexity assumptions and derive an explicit complexity bound.
result: The bound is independent of state dimension and depends only on convexity and Lipschitz constants, showing improved complexity over standard SDDP.
conclusion: BSDDP is efficient for structured strongly convex problems, especially when state dimension is large and number of stages is moderate.

title: Submodular Optimization With Applications To Decision And Control
authors: Shamak Dutta, Bahman Gharesifard, Stephen L. Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Submodular set functions, characterized by the diminishing-returns property, provide a unifying combinatorial framework for many subset-selection problems in decision and control. Although exact maximization is NP-hard in general, the structural properties of submodular functions enable simple greedy algorithms that achieve constant-factor approximation guarantees for monotone objectives, with randomized greedy-based variants extending such guarantees to the non-monotone case. This survey reviews the theory, algorithms, and applications of submodular optimization with a focus on systems and control. We cover the structural properties of submodular functions, including curvature and the submodularity ratio, the constraint families that arise in practice (matroids, knapsack, and [MATH]-systems), and the main approximation algorithms for monotone and non-monotone submodular maximization, with up-to-date approximation ratios and hardness results. We then survey applications across sensor scheduling, multi-agent coordination, robust submodular optimization, leader-follower systems, distributed submodular optimization, game theory, system theory, resource allocation, social networks, and informative path planning. The survey emphasizes practically implementable greedy-based algorithms and instance-dependent refinements via curvature and the submodularity ratio. We close with observations on canonical control-theoretic objectives: certain functionals are submodular (the log-determinant and rank of the controllability Gramian, and the log-determinant of the Kalman filter information matrix), whereas closely related objectives fail to be sub- or supermodular (the steady-state Kalman filter error covariance, and the average control energy obtained from the inverse Gramian). We also highlight the cross-cutting open directions that follow.
tldr: A survey of submodular optimization theory and algorithms with applications in control and decision systems.
motivation: Submodular set functions provide a framework for many subset-selection problems in decision and control, but their potential is not fully exploited in these fields.
method: The paper reviews structural properties of submodular functions, constraint families, and approximation algorithms, then surveys applications across sensor scheduling, multi-agent coordination, etc.
result: It identifies that certain control-theoretic objectives like log-determinant of controllability Gramian are submodular, while others like steady-state Kalman filter error covariance are not.
conclusion: Submodular optimization offers practical greedy algorithms with constant-factor guarantees for many control problems, but open directions remain.

title: A Dual Dynamic Programming Approach With Dimension-free Complexity For A Class Of Convex Optimization Problems
authors: Pablo Barros, Vincent Guigues, Jiaming Liang, Renato Monteiro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the complexity of a dual dynamic programming (DDP) method for solving a class of convex optimization problems with linear coupling constraints. Existing complexity results based on DDP depend on the dimensions of the state vectors and, in particular, grow exponentially with dimension. The goal of this paper is to establish a complexity bound that is independent of the dimension. Our approach first studies an unconstrained strongly convex problem and develops a flexible framework for DDP, called FDDP, for solving the associated dynamic programming equations, and establishes an iteration-complexity bound for it that is independent of the dimension. A dimension-independent complexity bound for the original linearly constrained problem is then obtained by applying FDDP to a corresponding unconstrained strongly convex problem obtained via smoothing and penalization. Inspired by the literature on bundle methods, FDDP updates lower approximations of cost-to-go functions through a generic procedure that includes both the classical multi-cut DDP and a new two-cut DDP variant as special cases. The two-cut variant maintains only two affine cuts per stage at each iteration, making it more memory-efficient while retaining the same theoretical guarantees. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate the practical behavior of multi-cut and two-cut DDP, including their dependence on problem parameters and their performance relative to a direct quadratic constraint reformulation.
tldr: This paper presents a dual dynamic programming method with dimension-independent complexity for a class of convex optimization problems with linear coupling constraints.
motivation: Existing DDP methods have complexity that grows exponentially with state dimension, limiting their applicability to high-dimensional problems.
method: The authors develop a flexible DDP framework (FDDP) that updates lower approximations of cost-to-go functions using a generic procedure, including multi-cut and a new two-cut variant, and apply it to a smoothed and penalized unconstrained strongly convex problem.
result: They establish an iteration-complexity bound for FDDP that is independent of the dimension, and the two-cut variant maintains only two affine cuts per stage, improving memory efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed FDDP methods achieve dimension-independent complexity and are validated numerically, showing practical effectiveness.

title: A Virtual Element Method For Elliptic Problems On Trimmed Background Meshes
authors: L. Beir\~ao Da Veiga, C. Canuto, R. H. Nochetto, G. Vacca, M. Verani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a two-dimensional piecewise [MATH] domain that cuts through a quasi-uniform fixed polygonal background mesh, for instance made of quadrilaterals. A simple procedure based on convex hulls gives rise to a rather small number of polygonal boundary elements of various shapes, including elements with small edges and large aspect ratios; this is the computational mesh for a virtual element method (VEM), a trimmed background mesh. We classify all possible geometric configurations and study their stability and approximability properties. This entails deriving robust stabilization mechanisms and interpolation estimates for anisotropic elements and elements with small cuts, as well as a weak maximum principle for enhanced virtual elements; these contributions have intrinsic interest for VEM theory on geometric flexibility. We prove that the resulting VEM is uniformly stable in [MATH], and also show optimal order-regularity error estimates in [MATH] and [MATH]. Insightful numerical experiments corroborate and complement our theory. The proposed method is suitable for treating ALE formulations of problems in moving domains.
tldr: This paper develops a virtual element method for elliptic problems on trimmed background meshes, focusing on geometric flexibility and numerical stability.
motivation: To handle complex geometries in moving domain problems without remeshing, using a fixed background mesh with cut elements.
method: Constructs polygonal boundary elements via convex hulls, classifies geometric configurations, and derives robust stabilization and interpolation estimates for anisotropic and small-cut elements.
result: Proves uniform stability and optimal error estimates in H1 and L2 norms, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed VEM is suitable for ALE formulations and moving domain problems, offering a flexible and accurate numerical approach.

title: Distributional Embeddings Of The First Limit Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman Space
authors: Juan Carlos Sampedro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the distributional self-embeddings of the centered first limit Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman space [MATH], [MATH]. Using a Boolean rigidity principle for its canonical independent-sum realization, we show that every such embedding is induced by a finite packing of Bernoulli factors. As a consequence, we also prove that [MATH] admits no proper non-zero internal compressions.
tldr: This paper classifies distributional self-embeddings of a specific Banach space using Boolean rigidity.
motivation: To understand the structure of distributional embeddings in the first limit Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman space.
method: Uses a Boolean rigidity principle for the canonical independent-sum realization of the space.
result: Every such embedding is induced by a finite packing of Bernoulli factors, and the space admits no proper non-zero internal compressions.
conclusion: The classification provides a complete characterization of distributional self-embeddings for this Banach space.

title: Koopman Modeling And Stabilization Of Discrete-Time Nonlinear Control Systems: Bilinearity On A Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space
authors: Jarod Morris, Xiuzhen Ye, Wentao Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite the popularity of Koopman modeling for nonlinear systems, in the presence of input variables, the evident nonexistence of a fully linear time-invariant model even in infinite dimensions makes Koopman-based control largely an open problem to date. Focusing on discrete-time systems in this paper, which eschews from using operator semigroup and infinitesimal generator notions, it is proven that nonlinear systems, if satisfying appropriate smoothness and regularity conditions, can be expressed exactly as bilinear dynamics, when the state variables and input variables are separately lifted into their reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). To account for the knowledge of an equilibrium point at the origin, the RKHS is defined by a linear--radial product kernel, and hence the functions belonging to this RKHS are spanned by the multiplications of component functions and Sobolev functions. The stabilization problem, namely the determination of a feedback law that causes a Lyapunov function (expressed as a kernel sum-of-squares form) to decrease, is then posed as an infinite-dimensional optimization problem over state-dependent conditional probability measures over the input space, solved via a discretization scheme.
tldr: This paper proposes a Koopman-based bilinear modeling and stabilization framework for discrete-time nonlinear control systems using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.
motivation: Koopman modeling for nonlinear systems with inputs lacks a fully linear time-invariant representation, making control design challenging.
method: The authors prove that under smoothness conditions, nonlinear systems can be exactly expressed as bilinear dynamics by lifting state and input variables into separate RKHSs with a linear-radial product kernel. Stabilization is formulated as an infinite-dimensional optimization over conditional probability measures.
result: The approach yields a bilinear model in infinite dimensions and a stabilization scheme via kernel sum-of-squares Lyapunov functions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for Koopman-based control of nonlinear discrete-time systems, though practical implementation requires discretization.

title: Supermodularity And Submodularity In Network Interdiction
authors: Bo Zhou, Ruiwei Jiang, Siqian Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a bilevel network interdiction problem, with an attacker interdicting (attacking) certain components of a network and a defender optimizing operations over the ensuing network. We study when the defender's optimal objective is submodular or supermodular with respect to the attacker's interdiction decisions, for optimizing the bilevel integer program more efficiently. We first consider the min-cost flow (MinCF) interdiction problem and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the supermodularity or submodularity to hold under three types of attacks, respectively on supplies/demands, flow capacities, and cost coefficients. We extend to other variants, including capacitated facility location, maximum flow (MaxF), and shortest path (SP) interdiction. The conditions hold under general network topologies and parameter settings, and depend solely on the locations of the attacks. We further incorporate additional network information (e.g., detailed parameters and special topologies) to establish less restrictive conditions. We also derive necessary and sufficient conditions for supermodularity or submodularity in SP and MaxF interdiction in series-parallel networks. Furthermore, we explore more challenging interdiction problems where the defender may make additional binary decisions (e.g., repairing or reinforcing the network) and identify conditions that preserve submodularity or recover supermodularity. Via extensive numerical studies with diverse types of attacks, we demonstrate an order-of-magnitude computational speedup achieved by exploiting these properties and generating valid inequalities, for solving network interdiction at scale.
tldr: This paper studies submodularity and supermodularity in bilevel network interdiction problems, focusing on computational optimization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Network interdiction problems are computationally challenging; exploiting structural properties like submodularity can speed up solution times.
method: The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for submodularity/supermodularity in min-cost flow, max flow, shortest path, and facility location interdiction under various attack types.
result: Conditions depend on attack locations and network topology; incorporating additional network information yields less restrictive conditions. Numerical experiments show order-of-magnitude speedups.
conclusion: Exploiting submodularity/supermodularity enables efficient solution of large-scale network interdiction problems.

title: Higher-order Diffusion Sampling Via Chebyshev Interpolation And Gauss--Seidel Iterations
authors: Meng Huang Bingyuan Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher-order ODE solvers have shown strong empirical promise for accelerating diffusion models through the probability flow ODE, but rigorous non-asymptotic guarantees for such acceleration remain limited. In this paper, we develop a Chebyshev--Gauss--Seidel higher-order sampler and establish a non-asymptotic convergence guarantee that allows the approximation order to grow logarithmically with the number of outer iterations. In the exact-score setting, up to logarithmic factors, the proposed sampler requires at most \[ d^{1+o_T(1)}\varepsilon^{-1/K_1} \] score functions to approximate the target distribution on \(^d\) within total variation distance \(\varepsilon\), where \(o_T(1)\to 0\) as \(T\to\infty\) and \(K_1>0\) is a sufficiently large constant. The analysis assumes only a polynomial second-moment bound on the target distribution, thereby relaxing the bounded-support condition imposed in existing higher-order theory. Moreover, the guarantee is robust to score and Jacobian estimation errors and does not require higher-order smoothness assumptions on the score estimates. Numerical experiments on anisotropic Gaussian mixture benchmarks support the predicted improvement in the accuracy--cost tradeoff under finite score-evaluation budgets.
tldr: This paper proposes a higher-order diffusion sampler using Chebyshev interpolation and Gauss-Seidel iterations with non-asymptotic convergence guarantees.
motivation: To accelerate diffusion models via higher-order ODE solvers while providing rigorous non-asymptotic guarantees that relax bounded-support assumptions.
method: Develops a Chebyshev-Gauss-Seidel higher-order sampler and analyzes its convergence using polynomial second-moment bounds and robustness to score estimation errors.
result: Achieves a score function complexity of d^{1+o_T(1)} ε^{-1/K_1} for TV distance ε, with logarithmic growth of approximation order in outer iterations.
conclusion: The proposed sampler offers improved accuracy-cost tradeoffs under finite score budgets, validated on anisotropic Gaussian mixtures.

title: Bidirectional Random Projections
authors: Luyuan Yang Chao Lan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper analyzes bidirectional random projections for ordinary least squares (OLS) regression under the fixed design setting. Let [MATH] be a sample and [MATH] be two properly distributed random projections. We develop an expected excess loss bound for the OLS estimator built on [MATH]. Compared to an established bound for OLS estimator built on [MATH], the gap is approximately [MATH], where [MATH] scales with [MATH] and can be negative for small [MATH]. Its implications are confirmed by numerical results on real-world data.
tldr: This paper studies bidirectional random projections for OLS regression, a classical statistical method, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To improve the efficiency of ordinary least squares regression using random projections.
method: The authors analyze the expected excess loss of an OLS estimator built on bidirectionally projected data and compare it to a unidirectional projection bound.
result: They derive a bound showing a gap that can be negative for small sample sizes, confirmed by numerical experiments.
conclusion: Bidirectional random projections can offer advantages over unidirectional ones in certain regression settings.

title: A Stochastic Gradient Algorithm For Non-separable Optimization With Convergence Guarantee
authors: Ruofan Wu Yingzhou Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-separable objectives in which the loss depend on dataset-level quantities. We introduce an SGD-style framework that employs two batch-gradient constructs: the ideal per-batch gradient `[MATH]' and a cached surrogate `[MATH]' for cases where full-data terms are expensive. Notably, in the sample-wise separable case, our method reduces to standard mini-batch SGD. Our main contribution is a unified local convergence theory: under mild smoothness and Jacobian-boundedness assumptions, we prove local linear convergence under local strong convexity and local [MATH] sublinear convergence under local convexity for both `[MATH]'-driven and `[MATH]'-driven updates. Crucially, these guarantees hold for fixed step sizes within explicitly characterized ranges; we provide explicit bounds showing how cache staleness, surrogate approximation error, batch size, and step size influence the convergence constants and allowable step-size ranges.
tldr: This paper proposes a stochastic gradient algorithm for non-separable optimization problems with convergence guarantees.
motivation: Many machine learning objectives involve dataset-level quantities that are not separable across samples, making standard SGD inapplicable. The authors aim to provide a practical algorithm with theoretical convergence guarantees.
method: The algorithm uses two batch-gradient constructs: an ideal per-batch gradient and a cached surrogate to handle expensive full-data terms. Convergence analysis is performed under smoothness and Jacobian-boundedness assumptions.
result: Local linear convergence under strong convexity and sublinear convergence under convexity are proven for fixed step sizes within explicit ranges. Bounds show how cache staleness, approximation error, batch size, and step size affect convergence.
conclusion: The proposed framework extends SGD to non-separable objectives while maintaining convergence guarantees, with potential applications in large-scale optimization.

title: Distributionally Robust Pca With Data-Adaptive Wasserstein Geometry
authors: Chuang Xu, Andrew T. A. Wood, Yanrong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a distributionally robust formulation of principal component analysis that minimizes worst-case reconstruction risk over distributions lying within a Wasserstein neighborhood of the empirical measure. The Wasserstein neighborhood, viewed as an ambiguity set of distributions, is adaptively calibrated through a transport matrix [MATH] to capture heterogeneous uncertainty across dimensions. The homogeneous case, in which G is a scalar multiple of the identity matrix, recovers classical PCA. Under a general transport matrix G, we derive a dual characterization of the associated minimax optimization problem and introduce a tractable surrogate objective function consisting of the square-root empirical reconstruction error plus a geometry-dependent residual exposure penalty. The exact and surrogate estimators are shown to be consistent for the population PCA subspace and asymptotically equivalent at the projector level. The transport geometry is allowed to be data adaptive, while the Wasserstein radius is calibrated via robust Wasserstein profile inference, yielding a data-driven radius of order [MATH]. Comprehensive theoretical guarantees are established, including consistency and local Grassmannian asymptotics exhibiting an explicit Wasserstein-induced drift determined by the limiting transport geometry and calibration level. Numerical experiments and a real-data application demonstrate that the proposed method can substantially improve finite-sample out-of-sample performance under structured covariance shifts, moderate contamination, and certain same-distribution regimes.
tldr: This paper develops a distributionally robust PCA method using Wasserstein ambiguity sets with data-adaptive transport geometry.
motivation: Classical PCA is sensitive to distributional shifts and outliers; the authors aim to improve robustness by minimizing worst-case reconstruction error over a Wasserstein neighborhood.
method: They formulate a minimax optimization problem with a Wasserstein ambiguity set calibrated via a transport matrix, derive a dual characterization, and propose a surrogate objective with a geometry-dependent penalty.
result: The proposed estimator is consistent for the population PCA subspace and asymptotically equivalent to the exact estimator, with explicit Wasserstein-induced drift in local Grassmannian asymptotics.
conclusion: The method improves out-of-sample performance under structured covariance shifts and contamination, offering a robust alternative to classical PCA.

title: Spectral And Computational Aspects Of A Regularized Fractional Laplacian For Non-local Diffusion On Graphs
authors: Mariarosa Mazza Alessandro Filippo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fractional Laplacian has been widely used to model non-local diffusion on graphs, allowing interactions that extend beyond immediate neighbors. However, it suffers from a structural inconsistency as it breaks compatibility with the topology of the original network. To address this issue, a combination of the standard and fractional Laplacians aimed at restoring compatibility while retaining the spectral richness of the fractional operator was recently proposed. In this work, we provide a thorough analysis of the diffusion properties of the resulting regularized operator. We prove that it yields superdiffusive behavior independently of whether the underlying graph is weighted or unweighted -a property not generally satisfied by other nonlocal Laplacian variants. An efficient construction of the regularized operator which preserves the same asymptotic computational cost of the fractional Laplacian is also given. Our numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and computational practicality of the regularized operator for modeling non-local diffusion on real-life networks.
tldr: This paper studies a regularized fractional Laplacian for non-local diffusion on graphs, focusing on spectral and computational aspects.
motivation: The fractional Laplacian on graphs suffers from structural inconsistency with the original network topology; the authors aim to restore compatibility while preserving spectral richness.
method: They propose a regularized operator combining standard and fractional Laplacians, prove its superdiffusive behavior, and provide an efficient construction with the same asymptotic cost as the fractional Laplacian.
result: The regularized operator yields superdiffusive behavior on both weighted and unweighted graphs, and numerical experiments show its effectiveness on real-life networks.
conclusion: The regularized operator is a practical and theoretically sound tool for modeling non-local diffusion on graphs.

title: A Nonlinear Snell Envelope Representation For Path-Dependent Controller-Stopper Games
authors: Magnus Perninge
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a finite-horizon, zero-sum stochastic differential game in which one player controls a path-dependent stochastic system, while the opponent is given the opportunity to terminate the game prematurely. We introduce a control randomization formulation, which allows us to establish that the upper and lower value functions coincide. Our approach also yields a representation of the common game value in terms of a nonlinear Snell envelope, where the underlying stopped process is given by the unique maximal solution of a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) with constrained jumps.
tldr: This paper studies a zero-sum stochastic differential game with path-dependent control and early termination, using control randomization and BSDEs.
motivation: To solve a finite-horizon zero-sum stochastic differential game where one player controls a path-dependent system and the other can terminate the game early.
method: Introduces a control randomization formulation to prove that upper and lower value functions coincide, and represents the common value via a nonlinear Snell envelope defined by a BSDE with constrained jumps.
result: The upper and lower value functions are equal, and the game value is given by a nonlinear Snell envelope of a stopped process that solves a BSDE with constrained jumps.
conclusion: The control randomization approach yields a tractable representation for path-dependent controller-stopper games.

title: Multiscale Modeling For Problems With High Contrast Heterogeneous Coefficients By The CEM-GMsFEM
authors: Eric T. Chung, Yalchin Efendiev, Xingguang Jin, Wing Tat Leung, Changqing Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This review paper provides a comprehensive overview of the Constrained Energy Minimizing Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (CEM-GMsFEM) for solving elliptic PDEs characterized by highly heterogeneous, high-contrast coefficients. We detail the construction of multiscale basis functions via spectral auxiliary spaces, combined with an oversampling strategy that enables localized computations and guarantees exponential error decay. Rigorous error estimates are outlined for reference to confirm the method's optimal convergence and robustness. Numerical simulations are provided to verify the exponential decay property of the multiscale basis functions. Additionally, we discuss and comment several up-to-date applications of CEM-GMsFEMs.
tldr: This paper reviews the CEM-GMsFEM method for solving elliptic PDEs with high-contrast heterogeneous coefficients, focusing on multiscale modeling and numerical analysis.
motivation: Efficiently solving PDEs with highly heterogeneous coefficients is challenging; the CEM-GMsFEM aims to provide a robust and accurate multiscale method.
method: The method constructs multiscale basis functions using spectral auxiliary spaces and an oversampling strategy to achieve localized computations and exponential error decay.
result: Rigorous error estimates confirm optimal convergence and robustness; numerical simulations verify the exponential decay property of the basis functions.
conclusion: CEM-GMsFEM is an effective approach for high-contrast heterogeneous problems, with potential applications in various fields.

title: Short-Range Iam Operations To Overcome Access Gaps Around Bologna Airport
authors: Jean-Claude Leb\`egue (OPTIM), Xuhao Gui (OPTIM), Daniel Delahaye
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Innovative Air Mobility (IAM) as a dedicated hub feeder and dispersal service for Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport (BLQ), addressing short-range airport-to-airport connectivity where scheduled fixed-wing services are inefficient and surface access is time-consuming. Demand is generated directly from BLQ's flight timetable via a staggered rolling-window model: arriving passengers become IAM-eligible after a 20-minute buffer (a baseline 70% ''staying'' share is considered and distributed across nearby airports using a gravity model), while feeder demand for departures is timestamped backward by IAM travel time plus a 2-hour pre-flight buffer. We build an IAM-only time-expanded network (airports as vertiports) and solve two sequential subproblems: passenger routing with A* to reveal edge-level demand pressure, followed by fleet dispatch with dynamic programming to schedule a finite IAM fleet. Using OAG schedules for 5 May 2024, we simulate 09:00-17:00 with a 50-vehicle fleet (10 seats, 30 m/s) and 5-minute windows. Results show large travel-time advantages versus rail for many links (e.g., BLQ-Il Ciocco: 46 min IAM vs. 237-294 min by train), while a few pairs remain competitive for rail (e.g., BLQ-Florence). Sensitivity to IAM speed and staying share quantifies how technology and adoption shape feasible coverage, timing feasibility, and hub accessibility, demonstrating the potential of IAM to strengthen BLQ's regional reach without altering airline schedules.
tldr: This paper studies short-range air mobility (IAM) as a feeder service for Bologna Airport, using a time-expanded network model and dynamic programming to schedule a fleet of electric aircraft.
motivation: To improve airport connectivity for short distances where traditional flights are inefficient and ground transport is slow.
method: A two-step approach: passenger routing via A* to estimate demand, then fleet dispatch with dynamic programming, using OAG flight schedules and a gravity model for demand distribution.
result: IAM offers significant travel-time savings over rail for many routes (e.g., 46 min vs. 237-294 min for BLQ-Il Ciocco), though some routes remain competitive for rail.
conclusion: IAM can effectively extend a hub airport's regional reach without altering airline schedules, with sensitivity to speed and adoption rates.

title: Dmsh: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework For All-Quad Mesh Generation
authors: Anirudh Kalyan, Cosmin Anitescu, Xiaoying Zhuang, Timon Rabczuk, Somdatta Goswami, Sundararajan Natarajan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating high-quality meshes for arbitrary geometries remains a fundamental bottleneck in computational engineering, often demanding heuristic tuning and semi-manual workflows. In this paper, we introduce Dmsh, a first fully automated reinforcement learning pipeline that unifies geometric decomposition and quadrilateral mesh generation within a single learning-based framework. Dmsh decomposes the problem through three coordinated agents handling topology simplification, geometric regularization, and mesh generation. The meshing process is formulated as a Markov Decision Process and solved using a parametric Soft Actor-Critic architecture with decoupled critics, enabling efficient exploration of a hybrid discrete-continuous action space. A curriculum learning strategy ensures scalability from simple domains to highly complex geometries, suppressing seed variance. By design, the recursive decomposition enables parallel meshing of subregions, yielding globally conforming all-quadrilateral meshes without post hoc correction. Across a wide range of benchmarks, Dmsh consistently outperforms existing methods in automation, robustness, and mesh quality, establishing a new paradigm for learning-based mesh generation.
tldr: This paper presents a reinforcement learning framework for generating quadrilateral meshes for arbitrary geometries, a topic in computational engineering.
motivation: Mesh generation is a bottleneck in computational engineering, often requiring manual tuning. The authors aim to automate and improve the process using multi-agent reinforcement learning.
method: They formulate mesh generation as a Markov Decision Process with three coordinated agents (topology, geometry, mesh) and use a parametric Soft Actor-Critic architecture with decoupled critics and curriculum learning.
result: The method outperforms existing methods in automation, robustness, and mesh quality across diverse benchmarks, producing globally conforming all-quadrilateral meshes.
conclusion: Dmsh establishes a new paradigm for learning-based mesh generation, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuity Of Projected Maps Of Heteroclinic Networks In $\mathbb{R}^{4}$
authors: David C Groothuizen Dijkema, Claire M Postlethwaite, Alastair M Rucklidge
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stability of robust heteroclinic cycles and networks is typically studied by constructing return maps and analysing their associated transition matrices. This analysis can be simplified with the network's projected map, derived by projecting the linear action of the transition matrix onto a simplex. This projection produces a piecewise-smooth map, which is one-dimensional for heteroclinic networks in [MATH]. We consider two such networks, the Kirk--Silber network and the [MATH]-clique network. For the Kirk--Silber network, the projected map is discontinuous on its switching manifold, while it is continuous for the [MATH]-clique network. In this paper, we address the dynamical phenomena that produce a discontinuity in the case of the Kirk--Silber network, and explain the value of the projected map at the switching manifold. We construct a completed return map near both networks, which captures the behaviour of all trajectories that begin near the network but may move away from it temporarily. We show that the discontinuity in the projected map of the Kirk--Silber network emerges due to two phenomena: first, there exists a discontinuity in a component of the completed return map in the limit as trajectories approach the Kirk--Silber network, as a result of the presence of a separatrix near the network, and, second, the procedure that defines the projected map. For the [MATH]-clique network, there is no such separatrix, and so no such discontinuity emerges. This analysis is a necessary step towards understanding the more complicated dynamics observed near heteroclinic networks of five or more equilibria.
tldr: This paper studies the continuity of projected maps of heteroclinic networks in R^4, focusing on the Kirk–Silber and 4-clique networks.
motivation: Understanding stability of robust heteroclinic cycles and networks is important in dynamical systems theory.
method: The authors construct completed return maps and analyze the projected maps derived from transition matrices.
result: The discontinuity in the projected map of the Kirk–Silber network arises from a separatrix near the network and the projection procedure, while the 4-clique network has no such discontinuity.
conclusion: This analysis is a step toward understanding dynamics near heteroclinic networks with five or more equilibria.

title: Disjointness Of Rescalings Of Smooth Area Preserving Flows On Surfaces
authors: Corinna Ulcigrai Przemys{\l}aw Berk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of [MATH], [MATH] of a flow [MATH] in the context of smooth flows preserving a smooth invariant measure, or, equivalently, locally Hamiltonian flows on compact orientable surfaces. We show that, when the genus of the surface is [MATH], almost every locally Hamiltonian flow with 2g-2 non-degenerate simple saddles is such that any distinct two rational rescalings [MATH] and [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH] of different absolute values, are disjoint. Previous results on disjointness of rescalings were available only for rescalings for locally Hamiltonian flows and their special flow representations in genus one. The result is proved using a criterion for disjointness based on the study of the distribution of Birkhoff sums of a special representation and in particular estimates on their exponential tails decay. A key novel geometric ingredient in the proof is the existence of a sequence of rigidity times which display what we call bounded-type rigidity, so that a large set of points comes back in time [MATH] with distance [MATH]. To produce such bounded-type rigidity times we exploit a particular way of degeneration of a translation surface to a flat torus for which the vertical flow has bounded-type rotation number.
tldr: This paper studies disjointness of rescalings of smooth area-preserving flows on surfaces, a topic in dynamical systems and ergodic theory.
motivation: To understand when two rescalings of a locally Hamiltonian flow are disjoint, extending results from genus one to higher genus surfaces.
method: Uses a criterion for disjointness based on distribution of Birkhoff sums and exponential tail decay, and constructs bounded-type rigidity times via degeneration of translation surfaces to flat tori.
result: Proves that for almost every locally Hamiltonian flow with 2g-2 non-degenerate simple saddles, any two distinct rational rescalings with different absolute values are disjoint.
conclusion: Establishes disjointness for a broad class of flows, contributing to the ergodic theory of surface flows.

title: On The Refined Properties Of Uniformly Quasi-greedy Bases
authors: Peiyang Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study some refined properties of uniformly quasi-greedy bases. In particular, we characterize the stability of uniformly quasi-greediness under scalings with bounded quotient and show that unconditionality is sufficient to guarantee this property. For the "isometric" case, i.e., when the uniformly quasi-greedy constant is [MATH], we prove that 1-uniformly quasi-greediness implies disjointness if the underlying norm is strictly monotone. We also introduce a stronger notion of quasi-greediness by requiring uniform order boundedness of the greedy sums over greedy orderings. The characterization and properties of such bases are derived along the lines of uniformly quasi-greedy bases.
tldr: The paper studies refined properties of uniformly quasi-greedy bases in functional analysis, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To characterize stability of uniformly quasi-greediness under scalings and introduce a stronger notion of quasi-greediness.
method: Mathematical proofs using properties of bases in Banach spaces, unconditionality, and strict monotonicity of norms.
result: Unconditionality ensures stability under scalings with bounded quotient; 1-uniformly quasi-greedy bases imply disjointness under strictly monotone norms; a stronger quasi-greediness notion is characterized.
conclusion: The results extend the theory of greedy bases but have no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Direct Data-Driven Approximate Optimal Control Of Nonlinear Input-Affine Systems
authors: Thulasi Mylvaganam Benita Nortmann
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we combine a data-driven system representation with a framework to systematically construct (approximate) solutions to nonlinear optimal control problems. By immersing the unknown dynamics into an extended state space, solutions are characterised via purely data-dependent algebraic conditions. This allows us to design dynamic state-feedback controllers with local stability and performance guarantees for unknown nonlinear, input-affine systems directly using data, without explicitly identifying the dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a data-driven method for approximate optimal control of nonlinear input-affine systems without explicit system identification.
motivation: Optimal control of unknown nonlinear systems is challenging; existing methods often require explicit model identification, which can be difficult or inaccurate.
method: The authors combine a data-driven system representation with an extended state space immersion to characterize solutions via purely data-dependent algebraic conditions, enabling direct design of dynamic state-feedback controllers.
result: The approach provides local stability and performance guarantees for unknown nonlinear input-affine systems using only data, without identifying the dynamics.
conclusion: The method offers a systematic way to construct approximate optimal controllers directly from data, with theoretical guarantees.

title: Derivatives Of Tensor Products And Applications To Spaces $C(K^n,X)$
authors: Leandro Candido
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we develop an abstract theory of derivatives for Banach spaces based on objects that we call . This framework encompasses both the Semadeni derivative and the recently introduced Semadeni--Pe{\l}czy\'nski derivative. More generally, suitable ideals of subsets of the dual space give rise to a broad family of derivatives within this setting. We establish addition and product formulas for these derivatives, showing that they behave naturally with respect to direct sums and injective tensor products. As an application, we compute iterated derivatives for a number of spaces [MATH] associated with scattered compacta, including scattered compact lines and compact trees. As a further application, we establish classification results for spaces of the form [MATH]. In particular, for uncountable ordinals [MATH] and [MATH], an integer [MATH], and Banach spaces [MATH] satisfying suitable rigidity assumptions, we prove that \[ C([0,\alpha]^n,X)\sim C([0,\beta]^n,X) \quad\quad C([0,\alpha])\sim C([0,\beta]). \] This extends Kislyakov's classification of spaces [MATH] and its vector-valued extension due to Galego to finite powers of ordinal intervals.
tldr: This paper develops an abstract theory of derivatives for Banach spaces and applies it to classify spaces of continuous functions on finite powers of scattered compacta.
motivation: To unify and extend existing derivative concepts (Semadeni, Semadeni-Pełczyński) and to classify Banach spaces of the form C(K^n, X) for scattered compacta K.
method: Introduces a general framework of derivatives based on ideals of subsets of the dual space, establishes addition and product formulas, and computes iterated derivatives for spaces associated with scattered compact lines and trees.
result: Extends Kislyakov's classification of C([0,α]) and its vector-valued version by Galego to finite powers of ordinal intervals, under suitable rigidity assumptions.
conclusion: The derivative framework provides a powerful tool for classifying Banach spaces of continuous functions on scattered compacta, with applications to ordinal intervals.

title: Safecloud: A Distributed, Encrypted Storage Cloud For Streaming
authors: Gregory Magarshak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Safecloud, a distributed, encrypted, self-pricing storage and streaming network whose storage and routing nodes never see plaintext and never hold keys. Each file is split into chunks, encrypted on the owner's device, and distributed across Drops (browser tabs storing ciphertext in IndexedDB) and Jets (federated routing servers). Only the owner, or an authorised grantee, can decrypt. We make five contributions: (1) A one-root key hierarchy: every key derives deterministically from a single root via HKDF, and owner and range-scoped grantee derive identical chunk keys (derivation agreement); a subtree key derives its range and nothing else (delegation containment). (2) Convergent content addressing: identical content yields identical ciphertext and identifiers, enabling deduplication without plaintext exposure, with identifiers binding authenticated ciphertext so a keyless Drop verifies integrity (blind verifiability). (3) Three parallel trees over one navigation path (Merkle for integrity, key-derivation for confidentiality, access for authorisation), with sound Merkle-verified retrieval. (4) The key tree doubles as a streaming index: a player derives each segment key in O(1), seeking by derivation, while parallel tracks (video, audio, captions) are independent subtrees unlockable per-track and per-segment, a combination we believe no prior encrypted-storage network offers. (5) Jets and Drops earn Safebux verifiably, kept honest by a one-signature proof-of-storage challenge under chilling-effect Proof-of-Corruption, a zero-sum economy that is significantly cheaper than Filecoin's proof-of-replication sealing (which is slow and provides no confidentiality). We give the architecture, cryptographic construction, a threat model, and an open-source reference implementation, stating precisely what is implemented versus designed.
tldr: Safecloud is a distributed encrypted storage and streaming network using a key hierarchy and convergent encryption for deduplication.
motivation: To provide a secure, decentralized cloud storage and streaming service where storage nodes never see plaintext or hold keys.
method: Files are split into chunks, encrypted client-side, and distributed across browser-based Drops and federated Jets; a one-root key hierarchy enables deterministic key derivation and delegation.
result: The system achieves deduplication without plaintext exposure, O(1) key derivation for streaming, and a proof-of-storage economy.
conclusion: Safecloud offers a practical encrypted storage network with novel key management and streaming features.

title: Hmaf: A Hierarchical Multi-Slot Gd-rtb Allocation Framework
authors: Tianxing Bu, Zhaoqi Zhang, Linyou Cai, Miao Xie, Shengri Xue, Tan Qu, Qianlong Xie, Xingxing Wang, Siqiang Luo, Gao Cong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In modern online advertising platforms, Guaranteed Delivery (GD) contracts coexist and bid with Real-Time Bidding (RTB) auctions. Recent approaches either decouple GD and RTB optimization or rely on heuristic priority rules, and thus fail to effectively balance short-term revenue maximization with long-term contract delivery under complex multi-slot delivery and impression constraints. To address these challenges, we propose HMAF (Hierarchical Multi-Slot Allocation Framework), a unified framework designed to optimize impression allocation in GD--RTB advertising platforms. HMAF employs the Plan--Calibrate--Execute paradigm as its core structure, and integrates offline constraint optimization with online decision-making, balancing offline GD resource planning, dynamically calibrating GD--RTB competitiveness, and making real-time listwise rank decisions across multi-slot environments. HMAF has been implemented in multiple marketing scenarios at Meituan, one of the world's largest online food delivery platforms, leading to a 3.72% increase in GD delivery rate and a 1.59% increase in total advertisement revenue.
tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchical framework for allocating impressions in online advertising platforms combining guaranteed delivery and real-time bidding.
motivation: Existing approaches fail to balance short-term revenue and long-term contract delivery under complex multi-slot constraints.
method: HMAF uses a Plan-Calibrate-Execute paradigm integrating offline constraint optimization, online calibration of GD-RTB competitiveness, and real-time listwise ranking.
result: Deployed at Meituan, achieving a 3.72% increase in GD delivery rate and 1.59% increase in total ad revenue.
conclusion: The framework effectively optimizes impression allocation in mixed GD-RTB environments.

title: IDP-Bench: Benchmarking Ability Of LLMs To Protect Personal Information In Interdependent Privacy Contexts
authors: Ayana Hussain, Soumya Sharma, Golnoosh Farnadi, Nicholas Vincent, H\'eber Hwang Arcolezi, Ulrich A\"ivodji
